items.passage:
I watched Katharina unwrap the brooch
beside a cup of coffee going cold,
the Hamburg trains exhaling on the platform
like tired men setting down their coats.
Her husband's, she said, pinned each winter
to the collar he wore for every leaving.
My hands, a bride's hands, were not certain
what a newcomer is owed of the dead,
or whether I had any right to touch it.
But she slid it over the marble tabletop
slowly, the way one offers bread to a sparrow,
and smiled the small smile of a woman
who has practiced letting go in private.
I held it until the metal warmed,
until it seemed, almost, to hold me back,
and Katharina's hand rested on my wrist.
Outside, a whistle; somewhere a door;
the waiter brushing crumbs into his palm.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Uneasy and guarded, as the speaker doubts her place in the family
Anxious overall, with only brief moments of warmth between the women
Tender overall, with an undercurrent of the speaker's uncertainty
Nostalgic and celebratory, as the women recall happier family days
items.explanation: 화자는 신부로서 고인의 물건을 받을 자격이 있는지 확신하지 못하는 불안을 잠시 드러내지만, 브로치를 '참새에게 빵을 건네듯' 천천히 밀어 주는 장면과 금속이 따뜻해져 자신을 안아 주는 듯한 장면, 손목에 얹힌 손이 이어지며 다정함이 지배적이 된다. 따라서 다정함을 중심으로 불안이 밑에 깔린 어조라고 한 C가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 불안만 말했고, B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었다. D의 축하·회상은 지문에 단서가 거의 없다.

items.passage: By the time Parvin unlocked the studio, the Tehran afternoon had already gone amber in the dusty skylight. Pearl and I had not stood in this room together since our last season on the stage, when we were young enough to rehearse lines while our aunt threw bowls at the wheel behind us. Her glazes still lined the shelves, blue as the costumes we used to borrow without asking. I laughed when Pearl found a cracked cup with both our initials scratched into its foot, and for a moment we were girls again, trading whispered cues. Yet the buyer's letter sat folded on the kiln, and neither of us had read it twice. Pearl ran her thumb along the cup's rough edge. I opened a window, and somewhere below, a vendor called out the price of pomegranates.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Quietly regretful, as the narrator dwells on the coming sale
Regretful overall, with fleeting moments of shared fondness
Playfully humorous, as the narrator mocks their younger selves
Fondly reminiscent, though shadowed by a lingering reluctance
items.explanation: 지문의 대부분은 함께 무대에 서던 시절, 숙모의 유약, 두 사람의 이니셜이 새겨진 컵을 보며 웃는 등 다정한 회상으로 채워져 있다. 그러나 가마 위에 접힌 매수자의 편지와 아무도 두 번 읽지 않았다는 서술이 망설임을 덧붙인다. 그래서 회상 중심에 주저함이 드리운 어조라고 한 D가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 아쉬움만, B는 비중을 뒤집었고, C의 조롱 섞인 유머는 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: I boarded Albert's barge on the Irwell expecting to stay ten minutes. Thirty years earlier he had torn my essay in half before the whole class, and I had carried that sound with me ever since. Now he moved slowly between coils of rope, offering tea in a chipped mug, and I kept my coat buttoned and my answers short. He did not apologize. Instead he showed me a shoebox of student papers he had kept, and mine was near the top, taped carefully along its tear. I set the mug down without drinking. Still, when he struggled with the stove, I reached over and lit it for him, and I did not leave when the ten minutes were up. Gulls settled on the roof of the cabin, and the water knocked against the hull.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Guarded and reserved, though gradually beginning to soften
Sympathetic and forgiving toward a teacher who has changed
Warm overall, with only traces of lingering caution
Mournful and elegiac, as the narrator grieves her childhood
items.explanation: 화자는 코트 단추를 채운 채 짧게 답하고 차를 마시지 않는 등 경계하는 태도를 여러 곳에서 보인다. 동시에 테이프로 붙인 에세이를 본 뒤 난로에 불을 붙여 주고 10분이 지나도 떠나지 않으며 마음이 조금씩 풀린다. 따라서 경계 중심에 점차 누그러지는 어조라는 A가 정답이다. B는 덜 두드러진 공감만, C는 비중을 뒤집었고, D의 애도는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: Dongsik mended nets on the Busan pier while Rania read Korean aloud from a child's workbook. When she stumbled over a word for sorry, he corrected her without looking up, then repeated it twice, more softly, as if testing it himself. She had come all this way after her father's funeral, carrying a letter Dongsik had written to his son years ago and never mailed. Every evening she asked whether she could read it to him yet, and every evening he said her vowels were still too American. Tonight, though, he slid the envelope across the crate between them and tapped one line with a tar-stained finger. Read only this part, he said. Rania bent over the paper, sounding out each syllable. Beyond them, a trawler backed slowly out of its berth, its lights blinking green and red.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Dongsik and Rania?
options: Rania is eager to grow closer, but Dongsik stays indifferent to her lessons.
Both are cautiously closing a distance, with Dongsik slowly trusting Rania.
Dongsik teaches Rania so that she will apologize to him for her father.
Rania regards Dongsik as a stern elder whose rules she follows without question.
items.explanation: 동식은 '미안하다'는 단어를 고쳐 준 뒤 스스로 시험하듯 부드럽게 되뇌고, 결국 부치지 못한 편지를 라니아에게 건네 한 줄을 읽게 한다. 라니아도 매일 저녁 편지를 읽어도 되는지 물으며 다가간다. 두 장면을 이어 보면 서로 조심스럽게 거리를 좁히고 동식이 점차 라니아를 믿게 되는 관계이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 라니아 쪽 감정만 반영했고, C는 사과의 방향을 뒤집었으며, D는 엄격한 어른이라는 통념에 기댄 선택지다.

items.passage: Nobody waits at a cemetery gate by accident. Tamika had been leaning on the iron bars for an hour when Ottavio's rental car finally pulled off the Delta road, dust rising behind it. He had moved north the spring her mother got sick, and she had stayed to do the nursing, the paperwork, the long nights. She did not mention any of that. She only said he had missed the service by two days. Ottavio nodded, took off his sunglasses, and handed her an envelope thick with receipts: every bill from the hospital, paid in his name, which she had never been told about. Tamika stared at them for a long time before tucking the envelope into her purse and taking his arm. Out past the gate, cotton fields ran flat to the tree line under a white sky.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Tamika and Ottavio?
options: Tamika resents Ottavio for leaving and no longer wishes to be his friend.
Ottavio feels that Tamika owes him for the sacrifices he made in secret.
They value their friendship despite strain over what each gave in the past.
They are old friends who drifted apart and now share only polite formality.
items.explanation: 타미카는 홀로 간병을 떠맡았던 일을 말하지 않고 장례식에 늦었다는 말만 하며 서운함을 드러낸다. 그러나 오타비오가 몰래 병원비를 내 왔다는 영수증을 건네자 오래 바라본 뒤 그의 팔을 잡는다. 두 장면을 이으면 희생의 불균형으로 긴장이 있지만 우정을 여전히 소중히 여기는 관계이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 타미카의 서운함만 반영했고, B는 빚진 방향을 뒤집었으며, D는 멀어진 옛 친구라는 통념에 기댄 선택지다.

items.passage: Years later I still remember Kostas sitting on the rim of the dry fountain in that Accra courtyard, cracking groundnuts with his thumb. He had been my grandfather's closest friend for forty years, and when I told him I had accepted the job in Toronto, he shook his head and said a man who leaves his grandfather's house leaves half his name behind. I expected him to stop speaking to me. Instead, the next morning, he was waiting by the gate with a folded map of the city I was going to, its streets already circled in pencil. These are the places my cousin trusts, he said, and pressed it into my hand without meeting my eyes. Overhead, weaver birds argued in the neem tree, and dust settled in the empty basin of the fountain.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Faisal and Kostas?
options: Faisal admires Kostas, but Kostas sees Faisal only as a reminder of a lost friend.
Faisal feels that Kostas must approve before he can accept the job abroad.
Kostas is a distant family acquaintance who has little say in Faisal's plans.
Kostas objects to Faisal's choice yet still supports him out of real affection.
items.explanation: 코스타스는 할아버지의 집을 떠나면 이름의 절반을 두고 가는 것이라며 파이살의 결정에 반대한다. 그러나 다음 날 아침 연필로 표시한 지도를 건네며 떠나는 길을 돕는다. 두 장면을 이어 보면 반대하면서도 애정으로 지지하는 관계이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 파이살 쪽 감정만, B는 허락의 방향을 바꿨으며, C는 지문의 40년 우정과 맞지 않는 통념적 관계다.

items.passage: Warm yeast, wet flour, and the hiss of the tandoor filled the Samarkand bakery long before dawn. Darius arrived each morning at four, though Aydin paid him only for six, and he swept the floor before she could ask. Neither of them spoke of the winter her husband had lent Darius's mother the money for a surgery, or of the fact that it had never been repaid. When he lifted the heaviest trays, she pretended not to notice. When she slipped an extra round of bread into his satchel, wrapped in a cloth embroidered with her husband's initials, he pretended the same. Once, he began to say something about his mother, and Aydin handed him a sack of sesame seeds before he could finish. Through the window, the blue dome of the mosque slowly took shape against the brightening sky.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Aydin and Darius?
options: They share an unspoken understanding that each honors through small acts.
Darius feels deeply indebted to Aydin, who has no idea of his family's loan.
Aydin is quietly working to repay a debt she believes she owes to Darius.
Aydin is a strict employer and Darius a hired boy who simply does his job.
items.explanation: 다리우스는 돈을 받는 시간보다 일찍 와서 무거운 쟁반을 들고, 아이딘은 모르는 척하며 빵을 몰래 가방에 넣어 준다. 다리우스가 어머니 이야기를 꺼내려 하자 아이딘이 참깨 자루를 건네 말을 막는 장면도 둘 다 빚 이야기를 피하며 배려한다는 것을 보여 준다. 따라서 말하지 않는 이해를 작은 행동으로 지키는 관계라는 A가 정답이다. B는 한쪽 감정만 반영했고 아이딘이 모른다는 점도 틀렸으며, C는 빚의 방향을 뒤집었고, D는 고용 관계라는 통념에 기댄 선택지다.

items.passage: We waited on the bench nearest the Havana ferry ramp, Father Emiliano in his faded cassock and I, Cleotilde, with a ticket my cousin had bought me to leave by morning. A thick mooring rope lay coiled at our feet, salt-stiff and frayed where it had rubbed the pier for years. I had not been to Mass in a decade, and I told him so, as if he did not already know. He only nodded at the rope. Every boat that docks here, he said, gets tied with that same line, and it never seems to break. When the gangway lowered, a deckhand looped the rope around a post, and the ferry strained against it, groaning, held fast. I folded my ticket into a smaller square. Even after I stood, my eyes kept returning to that worn rope, knotted so many times it had stopped looking like rope at all.
items.question: In the text, the mooring rope most likely represents
options: the dangers of the sea crossing that Cleotilde is afraid to face.
the ties to home and faith that still hold Cleotilde as she leaves.
the strict church rules that Father Emiliano wants her to obey.
the weariness of the workers who have labored at the terminal.
items.explanation: 밧줄은 지문에서 여러 번 반복되는데, 신부는 미사를 떠난 클레오틸데의 말에 대답 대신 밧줄을 가리키며 '끊어지지 않는다'고 말하고, 배는 떠나려 당기지만 밧줄에 붙들린다. 클레오틸데는 표를 더 작게 접고 일어선 뒤에도 밧줄을 계속 바라본다. 이를 이어 보면 밧줄은 떠나려는 그녀를 여전히 붙드는 고향과 신앙의 끈이므로 B가 정답이다. A의 바다 위험, C의 교회 규칙, D의 노동자 피로는 지문의 단서와 연결되지 않는다.

items.passage: Milena held the dustpan while her mother swept, as she had every Saturday since she was nine. Marlon's barbershop on Brīvības Street closed at six, and her mother, who had cut hair there for twenty years, never let anyone else sweep up. Tonight they were supposed to be choosing wedding napkins, and the catalog lay open on a barber chair, but the broom kept moving in its old pattern: under the mirrors, around the coat rack, toward the door. Brown curls, gray tufts, a child's blond fringe. You'll have your own floors soon, her mother said, not looking up. Milena tipped the pan into the bin. Then she took the broom from her mother's hands and finished the last corner herself, the way she had seen it done a thousand times. Marlon, counting the till, pretended not to watch. Her mother sat down at last and turned a page of the catalog.
items.question: In the text, the act of sweeping the shop floor most likely represents
options: the tiresome duties that Milena hopes to escape by marrying.
the mother's refusal to accept that her daughter is getting married.
a shared ritual binding Milena to her mother as their lives change.
Marlon's strict expectations for how his barbershop should be kept.
items.explanation: 청소는 밀레나가 아홉 살 때부터 매주 토요일 엄마와 함께해 온 의식으로 소개되고, 결혼 준비 중에도 비질은 옛 패턴대로 이어진다. 엄마가 '곧 너만의 바닥이 생길 것'이라고 말한 뒤 밀레나가 비를 받아 엄마가 하던 방식대로 마지막 구석을 마친다. 이를 종합하면 비질은 삶이 바뀌는 순간에도 두 사람을 이어 주는 공유된 의식이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 탈출하고 싶은 일로, B는 결혼 거부로, D는 마를론의 기준으로 잘못 해석했다.

items.passage:
Three rules of the theater in the off-season:
no films, no tickets, no one asks why you came.
Nandi sat in row nine in his pressed uniform,
his transfer papers folded inside his cap,
and Neema, his sister, swept popcorn husks
from a Nairobi rainy season months gone.
Above them the screen hung blank and white,
a field no one had walked across yet.
He had watched worse things than films on other walls.
She flicked the projector on by accident,
and light poured out with nothing in it,
just dust turning slowly in the beam.
He did not ask her to switch it off.
He stood, walked to the stage, and laid his palm
flat against the empty screen,
as if it were warm, as if it might hold
whatever he decided to put there.
Neema kept sweeping. The cap stayed on the seat.
items.question: In the text, the blank screen most likely represents
options: the violent memories that Nandi cannot stop replaying in his mind.
the loneliness of the theater during the long off-season months.
the films that Neema wishes the theater could afford to show again.
an unwritten future Nandi is beginning to let himself imagine.
items.explanation: 빈 스크린은 '아직 아무도 걸어 보지 않은 들판'에 비유되고, 낸디는 그 위에 손을 대며 자신이 무엇을 놓을지 정할 수 있다는 듯 행동한다. 전출 서류가 든 모자를 의자에 두고 떠나는 마지막 장면도 그가 조용히 마음을 바꾸고 있음을 암시한다. 따라서 빈 스크린은 그가 상상하기 시작한 아직 쓰이지 않은 미래이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 '다른 벽에서 본 더 나쁜 것들'이라는 표현을 오해했고, B와 C는 배경 소재에만 기댄 해석이다.

items.passage: Years later, at a crowded wedding hall in Rotterdam, I saw a paper crane tucked behind a place card, and I thought at once of Grant. He had been my night patient for three weeks on the cardiac ward, and every evening when I came to check his monitors, there was a new crane folded from a menu card on his tray. The other nurses teased me that he wanted something: a larger dose, an extra blanket, my phone number. I waited for the request. It never came. On his last night he asked only whether I had kept them, and when I said yes, all nineteen, he closed his eyes and smiled. I left the cranes on my windowsill for years, where they faded in the sun but never fell. At the wedding, I picked up the one by my plate and held it as the music started.
items.question: In the text, the paper cranes most likely represent
options: a gratitude Grant offered without expecting anything back.
a quiet request that Grant was too embarrassed to say aloud.
the boredom Grant felt during his long nights in the hospital.
the playful teasing that Freja endured from the other nurses.
items.explanation: 동료 간호사들은 학들이 무언가를 바라는 신호라고 놀렸지만, 화자가 기다린 요청은 끝내 오지 않았다. 마지막 밤에도 그랜트는 학을 간직했는지만 묻고 미소 지었으며, 화자는 학들을 오랫동안 창턱에 두었다. 이를 이어 보면 학은 대가를 바라지 않은 감사의 표시이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 동료들의 의심을 그대로 따른 오답이고, C의 지루함과 D의 놀림은 학의 의미를 소재 수준에서만 해석했다.

items.passage: On the evenings after we closed the shop early, Hala and I took the old ball down to the dirt field behind the Marrakesh tannery. Its leather had split along one seam, and every week Hala stitched it again with waxed thread from our father's spool, though a new ball cost less than an afternoon of his time. We never spoke of the ledger, of the rent three months late, or of the doctor's letter about our father that I had hidden in the drawer under the receipts. We just passed the ball back and forth while the call to prayer rose over the walls. It was heavier each time, the stitches thicker, the shape a little more lopsided. Still neither of us suggested buying another. When it rolled into the shadows near the goalposts, Hala jogged after it, and I waited, the dust turning pink in the last of the light.
items.question: In the text, the repeatedly stitched ball most likely represents
options: the brothers' childhood dreams of becoming professional players.
the brothers' unspoken effort to keep a failing life intact together.
Hala's wish to save money by avoiding any unnecessary purchases.
the father's skill as a craftsman, which the brothers have inherited.
items.explanation: 형제는 장부나 밀린 임대료, 숨겨 둔 의사 편지에 대해 말하지 않으면서 매주 터진 공을 다시 꿰매 함께 차고, 공은 점점 무거워지고 비뚤어지지만 누구도 새 공을 사자고 하지 않는다. 이 공은 망가져 가는 가게와 가족의 현실을 말없이 붙들고 버티는 두 사람의 노력과 겹쳐진다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 축구라는 소재만, C는 '새 공이 더 싸다'는 서술과 어긋나고, D는 아버지의 실을 쓴다는 세부를 과장했다.

items.passage: Who gives a widow a shovel for her seventy-fifth birthday? Zawadi had asked herself that for a week, ever since Theo arrived with the long box tied in green ribbon. Since his grandfather's death she had not left the flat, and she suspected the gift was a polite way of telling her to stop sitting in the dark and find some useful chore. So the shovel stood in the corner of the kitchen like an accusation, and each time she passed it, she looked away. On Sunday Theo came back and took her by the arm to the community garden above the Marseille harbor. In the far bed, under a fig tree, a small wooden sign carried his grandfather's name. He kept this plot for forty years, Theo said. Nobody else should dig it. Zawadi stood very still, then held out her hand for the shovel he had carried up the hill.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “like an accusation” most nearly suggests that the shovel
options: was too heavy and awkward for Zawadi to use comfortably.
reminded Zawadi of the tools her husband once kept in the flat.
seemed to Zawadi to reproach her for the way she was grieving.
had been chosen by Theo to express his anger toward Zawadi.
items.explanation: 자와디는 남편이 죽은 뒤 집 밖에 나가지 않았고, 삽 선물이 어둠 속에 앉아 있지 말고 일을 찾으라는 완곡한 말이라고 의심했다. 그래서 삽이 구석에 '비난처럼' 서 있고 그녀는 지날 때마다 눈을 피한다. 이 문맥에서 표현은 삽이 그녀의 애도 방식을 나무라는 것처럼 느껴졌다는 뜻이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 비유를 물리적 무게로 오해했고, B는 지문에 없는 연상이며, D는 테오의 의도가 화가 아니었다는 결말과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Josiah had bought fish from Ephraim every Friday for two years and had never once seen the old man smile. Everyone on Mill Street said he was a miser who shorted his scales and cursed at children. So Josiah nearly dropped his notebook the Tuesday night he walked into the adult English class at the Ohio language school and found Ephraim at the chalkboard, patiently drilling six new arrivals on the names of vegetables. The teacher explained afterward that Ephraim had come to the town forty years ago knowing no English, and that he had taught the night class for free ever since, on one condition: that no one at the market ever learn of it. His temper, she said, was a fence he had built himself, high enough that no one would come to thank him. Josiah watched the old man erase the board in long, careful strokes.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a fence he had built himself” most nearly suggests that Ephraim's temper is
options: a habit he acquired from the harsh customers at the market.
a sign of the frustration he feels while teaching new arrivals.
a flaw that his neighbors have unfairly exaggerated over time.
a barrier he keeps up on purpose to hold gratitude away.
items.explanation: 에프라임은 수업을 무료로 가르치면서 시장 사람들이 절대 알지 못하게 하라는 조건을 걸었고, 교사는 그의 성질이 아무도 고맙다고 찾아오지 못할 만큼 높게 쌓은 '울타리'라고 말한다. 따라서 이 비유는 감사를 멀리하려고 그가 일부러 세워 둔 장벽을 뜻하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 '스스로 지었다'는 점과 어긋나고, B는 그가 인내심 있게 가르친다는 서술과 맞지 않는다. C는 이웃의 소문을 다루지만 비유가 강조하는 의도적 선택을 놓쳤다.

items.passage:
We were twelve in a cabin outside Dhaka
the winter snow came, absurd and soft,
sealing the road the festival van would use.
Arjun had promised word by evening:
whether the orchestra would play in the capital
or fold its music stands for good.
Meera, the youngest, held her violin unopened
in its case across her knees.
No one rehearsed. No one ate the rice.
By dusk the silence tuned itself to a single string,
and every face leaned toward the radio
the way a bow leans toward a note.
Arjun paced from the stove to the window,
his baton tucked behind one ear,
forgetting it was there.
Meera unlatched the case at last,
not to play, only to see the wood,
while snow kept falling past the glass.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the silence tuned itself to a single string” most nearly suggests that
options: the group's attention narrowed to one shared, anxious focus.
the musicians began to rehearse a single piece together quietly.
the snowstorm outside had muffled every sound except one.
Meera's violin had gone out of tune in the cold cabin.
items.explanation: 지문은 소식을 기다리며 아무도 연습하거나 먹지 않는 긴장된 장면을 그리고, 바로 뒤에 모든 얼굴이 활이 음을 향하듯 라디오 쪽으로 기울었다고 서술한다. 따라서 '침묵이 한 줄에 맞춰 조율되었다'는 표현은 모두의 신경이 하나의 불안한 초점으로 좁혀졌다는 뜻이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 '아무도 연습하지 않았다'는 서술과 어긋나고, C는 눈을 문자 그대로의 소리 차단으로 읽었으며, D는 비유를 악기의 실제 조율로 오해했다.

items.passage: Katerina drove the number 12 bus past the harbor in Thessaloniki every morning, and every morning Eda boarded at the stop beside the shoe repair stall. One spring she stepped on carrying a pair of men's brown oxfords, the heels worn to a slant. Her husband had died in January. She had brought the shoes to the cobbler three times, she told Katerina, asking him to replace the soles, then the laces, then the stitching along the toe. Each time he did the work without complaint, and each time she took them home and set them by the door, where no one would wear them. Mending them, Eda said, was like stitching a new sentence onto a closed book. Katerina said nothing and waited at the green light a moment longer than she needed to, so Eda could sit down. Then she pulled away from the curb into the traffic along the sea.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “stitching a new sentence onto a closed book” most nearly suggests
options: a craft that requires more skill than the cobbler possesses.
an effort to extend something that has already come to an end.
a way of recording the husband's life story for others to read.
a task that Eda finds tedious and wishes she could abandon.
items.explanation: 에다는 남편이 죽은 뒤 아무도 신지 않을 구두를 세 번이나 고쳐 문 옆에 둔다. 이 행동을 '닫힌 책에 새 문장을 꿰매 붙이는 것'에 빗댄 것은 이미 끝난 삶에 무언가를 덧붙이려는 시도라는 뜻이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 구두장이가 불평 없이 일을 해냈다는 서술과 맞지 않고, C는 '책'을 문자 그대로 기록으로 읽었다. D는 그녀가 스스로 반복해 수선을 맡긴다는 점과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Rumors travel faster than ferries. I learned that the autumn I clerked for Ingeborg, a retired judge who still walked the Bergen promenade each morning in a black wool coat. Someone at the fish market had whispered that her late brother once took bribes, a story she had disproved in court decades earlier and never bothered to repeat. Most people shrugged it off. But it reached her niece, who had just been appointed to the bench and who had always believed her uncle was a man without stain. By the next morning, the rumor had found the one door left unlocked, and the niece stopped answering Ingeborg's calls. I, Ingrid, carried the old court file to the niece's office myself, wrapped in brown paper. Ingeborg did not ask whether I had delivered it. She only stood at the railing, watching the gulls ride the wind above the harbor.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the rumor had found the one door left unlocked” most nearly suggests that the rumor
options: had been spread deliberately by someone inside Ingeborg's household.
was finally proven false once it reached the courts in Bergen.
reached the one person most open to being hurt by it.
caused Ingeborg to lock herself away from her neighbors.
items.explanation: 대부분의 사람은 소문을 대수롭지 않게 넘겼지만, 삼촌을 흠 없는 사람이라 믿어 온 조카에게 닿자 그녀는 잉에보르의 전화를 받지 않게 된다. 이 맥락에서 '잠기지 않은 유일한 문을 찾았다'는 표현은 소문이 가장 상처받기 쉬운 사람에게 닿았다는 뜻이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '문'을 집안 내부로 문자 그대로 읽었고, B는 지문에 없는 결과이며, D는 문을 잠그는 주체를 잉에보르로 바꾼 오답이다.

items.passage: Mumbai was loud that monsoon, but nothing was louder than the quiet at the noodle stall on the corner of Khetwadi Lane. After the mother left for her sister's village and did not return, the old noodle man and his stubborn son kept the stall open as if she had only stepped out for onions. Each night the son set out three bowls, and each night the father filled only two, and neither said a word. Sharda, who sold tea at the next stall, told her niece Priya that the pair were stirring the same pot of silence, and that it would boil over one day. Priya laughed, for the men seemed calm enough. But the tale goes that on the first dry evening of the year, the son set out two bowls, and the father, seeing it, set down his ladle and wept. Steam rose from the pot and drifted toward the lamps.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “stirring the same pot of silence” most nearly suggests that the father and son
options: were too busy preparing food to speak during the crowded evenings.
had quarreled bitterly and refused to work at the same stall again.
were secretly planning together to bring the mother back home.
were jointly keeping up an unspoken avoidance of their loss.
items.explanation: 아들은 매일 그릇 세 개를 놓고 아버지는 두 개만 채우면서도 둘 다 아무 말을 하지 않으며, 어머니가 잠깐 나간 것처럼 가게를 계속 연다. 샤르다가 이를 '같은 침묵의 냄비를 젓는다'고 표현하고 언젠가 끓어 넘칠 것이라 한 것은 두 사람이 상실을 말하지 않고 함께 피하고 있다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 비유를 실제 요리로 읽었고, B는 함께 가게를 지킨다는 서술과 어긋나며, C는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: "Take your time," Omar said, and then, for once, he did not say anything else. For years he had ______ silence the moment it appeared in his classroom, rushing in with hints, jokes, and second explanations before any student could finish thinking. Yasmin had not spoken a word aloud in his class since September. Every morning they waited together at the mountain bus stop above Cairo, and every morning he filled the cold air with questions she answered with a shrug. Today he held back. He counted the passing cars, studied the haze over the city, and let the quiet stretch until it felt almost unbearable. Then Yasmin pointed at a hawk circling above the ridge and said its name in English, softly, as if testing the word. Omar nodded and kept his eyes on the bird. Down the road, the bus rounded the last bend, its horn echoing off the rocks.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: smothered
welcomed
observed
prolonged
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 오마르는 학생들이 생각을 마치기도 전에 힌트와 농담, 추가 설명으로 끼어들었다고 하고, 매일 아침 질문으로 공기를 채웠다는 서술도 이어진다. 따라서 침묵이 생기자마자 '덮어 눌러 버렸다'는 뜻의 A가 가장 논리적이다. B와 D는 오늘에야 침묵을 견딘 변화와 반대되는 습관을 나타내고, C는 침묵을 서둘러 메우는 행동의 의미를 담지 못한다.

items.passage: We rehearsed on the lakeside dock in Chiang Mai every evening for a week before the lantern festival, when our crew would row the long boat past the crowds in perfect time. Aung, our foreman, had hired Thida only that month, and on the first night she counted every stroke aloud, glancing at the rest of us before each pull and lifting her oar a beat too late. Aung said nothing. He only moved her to the seat behind him, where she could watch his shoulders. By the sixth evening she had stopped counting and stopped looking around; her strokes were ______, rising and falling with ours as though she had rowed beside us for years. Aung grunted once, which from him counted as praise. Across the water, the first paper lanterns drifted up from a temple roof and hung above the trees.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: tentative
unhesitating
ornamental
hurried
items.explanation: 첫날 티다는 노를 저을 때마다 소리 내어 세고 주변을 살피다 한 박자 늦었지만, 여섯째 날에는 세는 것도 둘러보는 것도 멈추고 오래 함께 저어 온 사람처럼 박자를 맞춘다. 따라서 망설임 없이 자연스럽게 젓는다는 B가 가장 적절하다. A는 첫날의 모습에 해당해 변화와 맞지 않고, C는 동작의 장식성을 말해 문맥과 무관하며, D는 다른 사람들과 박자가 맞았다는 서술과 어긋난다.
